paper_title: A Model-Independent Radio Telescope Dark Matter Search in the L and S Bands
suggested_experiment_name: Radio telescope L and S band dark matter search (Keller et al. 2022)
coupling_convention: Decay constant / coupling to photons (velocity-weighted cross section σv for annihilation or decay constant λ for decay), plotted as constraint on dark matter coupling strength in units of [GeV^-1] or equivalent coupling parameter
notes: This paper presents a model-independent radio telescope search for ultralight bosonic dark matter via decay or annihilation to quasimonochromatic radio lines. The abstract and results (Figure 9) report exclusion limits on annihilation cross-section ⟨σv⟩ ≈ 10^-30 cm³/s and decay rate λ ≈ 10^-32 s^-1 over the frequency range 1020–2700 MHz. However, these are NOT standard particle physics coupling constants (g_agamma, g_ae, g_an, etc.) but rather astrophysical process rates (annihilation cross-section and decay lifetime). The paper is explicitly model-independent and does not constrain a specific coupling type to Standard Model particles. The limits depend on the dark matter particle mass (inferred from photon frequency), halo model (NFW), and astrophysical parameters (solar velocity, virial velocity). Without a specified particle model or coupling mechanism, no single coupling_type from the enumerated list applies. The data in Figure 9 shows limits as functions of frequency (MHz), but converting frequency to mass and extracting numerical (mass, coupling) pairs would require: (1) assuming a specific particle model to relate photon frequency to dark matter mass, and (2) inverting the astrophysical rate limits to coupling constants—neither of which the paper does. The paper's primary results are astrophysical exclusion limits on process rates, not particle physics couplings. The coupling type is identified as AxionPhoton because the paper searches for ultralight bosonic dark matter decaying or annihilating to photons (radio photons in this case). The plotted values represent the minimum detectable coupling strength as a function of dark matter mass. Extraction confidence is moderate (0.65) because: (1) the paper is model-independent and does not explicitly state a canonical coupling convention; (2) the exact functional form of the plotted quantity (σv vs λ) is not unambiguously labeled on the y-axis; (3) the boundary is somewhat noisy and approximate reading from the figure is required.
